_comment: Template joint orientation rules (A1 / A2 / A3).
Everything is computed the same way: aim one local axis at something and
point another local axis at a hint (a pole target, or a world axis).
Order matters and the tool enforces it (plan 4-6):
1 mirror        - the right side needs positions before anything is aimed,
and A2 reads the mirrored pole targets
3 pole_chains   - A2, arms and legs (+ tail / preserve)
4 position_only - forced last so world-zero rotation wins over the mirror
'tail' handles the end joint, which an IK solver never rotates (plan 2-1):
legs -> a tail group, arms -> "preserve" (leave it exactly as it is).
"preserve" is a DECISION, not a gap - see plan 4-9.

aim_groups.name: spine
aim_groups.comment: A1. forward +X at the next joint, +Z toward world +Z. The checkbox replaces this with world zero.

aim_subtrees.name: fingers_l
comment: Every joint under the left hand: forward +X at its own child, +Y toward
world +Y. A leaf finger tip has no child, so it copies its parent.
The right hand is not listed here - it is mirrored from this one, and that
mirror has to run AFTER this (see mirror.behavior with stage 'late').
Pole targets for the foot and toe IK. After everything is oriented they sit
10 along their own +Z, measured from their parent (translate = 0,0,10).
This is the only rule that moves a joint, which is why the step is called

behavior.comment: A3 arm. Mirrors the whole arm including the 19 finger joints. Runs first; A2 overwrites upperarm/lowerarm afterwards.

comment: The right fingers. This one runs LATE - after aim_subtrees has oriented
the left hand. The early mirror above would copy the left fingers before
they are aimed, so their orientation would be whatever the user left.

position_pairs.comment: A3 leg. Position only - the orientation is rebuilt by A2 (forward +X, not a behavior mirror).

position_only.comment: A3. Position mirrored onto the _r side, world rotation zero on BOTH sides. Runs last.
